ember.note: Scarce by contract: active state and primary action only.

faint.note: Lifted from #5a6185, which measured 3.21:1 on the void behind 11-13px text. The shipped value clears 4.5:1.

display.purpose: The hero line only, set at wdth 64% so four words hold a line that would otherwise take six.

figure.purpose: Standalone queried numerals in the stat band, wdth 76% and tabular.

body.purpose: Paragraphs, capped at 62ch in the hero and 68ch in specification rows.

label.purpose: Controls, nav, band names, stage names. Uppercase, tracked 0.16-0.20em.

micro.purpose: Margin instrumentation: readout caption, environment readout, scroll rail.

code.purpose: JetBrains Mono, reserved for file paths, line numbers and scan output.

shadows.name: control-lift
shadows.purpose: Under the primary control only. Offset down with negative spread, so it reads as depth rather than glow.

shadows.name: panel-drop
shadows.purpose: Desktop-only ambient drop beneath the widest panels (scan output, list view). Black and soft, never tinted.

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: Opacity-only entrance for things that appear where nothing was.

motion.name: slide-in-right
motion.purpose: Panels entering from the right edge.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: The still field's slow transform drift, for phones and reduced-motion visitors.

motion.name: radar-sweep
motion.purpose: The brand mark's conic sweep, brightness peaking at the leading edge.

motion.name: blip
motion.purpose: A pulsing live indicator. Expanding ring, lilac at 50% mix.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Control hover: border and label to ember, arrow nudged 4px right.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Stillness rather than a slower version of the same motion. Load-bearing, not decorative.

narrative.overview:
debtradar renders a codebase the way a nowcast renders an atmosphere. The hero is not a backdrop behind a claim — it is a particle field whose filaments are where risk concentrates, cold at the left where the copy sits and running hot toward the lower right. Everything above the field is instrumentation read off that weather: a numbered stage index pinned to the left margin, tiny tracked labels at the edges, a live readout in the position a loader would occupy, a scroll rail at the right. The page is dark, cold, and mostly empty, and the one warm thing on it is the thing you are meant to press.

The density is instrument-panel rather than marketing-page. Structure is carried by hairlines and by background seams — a one-pixel grid gap showing the edge colour through a grid of panels — not by cards floating on shadow. Type does the heavy lifting through a width axis rather than through more families: one variable grotesk set genuinely narrow at architectural scale for display, and genuinely wide and tiny for labels. Monospace is reserved for things that are literally code: file paths, line numbers, scan output.

Confirmed rejections: the category default of a dark hero with a terminal screenshot beside a "ship faster" headline, and its opposite, the neutral claim-and-screenshot page. The filled pill button is rejected. The equal-card feature grid is rejected — it shipped once and was replaced by a specification list. The previous near-black-plus-mint identity is removed outright: there is no mint and no green in this world.
keyCharacteristics: Three cold grounds (void, ink-deep, night), two structural colours, one incandescent accent.
One variable grotesk driven on its width axis; 64% for display, 76–80% for figures and headlines.
Hairline rectangles with a drawn arrow for every control; no filled pills.
A four-band severity ramp lifted from the field's own filaments.
Every public figure queried from the database, never typed.
The shader is desktop-and-motion-gated by a decision that precedes its import.

rules.name: The One Heat Rule
rules.body: Ember appears at most twice in a viewport, and only as the active state or the primary action. A third simultaneous spend is a regression; it was raised as one and corrected by returning the secondary control to a lilac rest state.

rules.name: The Four-Band Rule
rules.body: The severity ramp is the field's own ramp — steel, lilac, violet, ember — so a band's colour and its position in the field mean the same thing. There are four bands because a fifth would have to come from outside that ramp.

rules.name: The Written Band Rule
rules.body: Band colour never carries meaning alone. The band name is always set in words beside its mark, because on this ramp violet-versus-ember is the difference between high and critical.

rules.name: The Cold Ground Rule
rules.body: Every ground is one of void, ink-deep, or night. Warmth on this page is information, never atmosphere.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Condensed and extended come from the one loaded family's wdth axis, never from a second font file. The axis must be requested at load (axes: ["wdth"]); without it every font-stretch in the page silently does nothing.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number read against another number down a column — counts, risk scores, line numbers, index numerals — carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums via the .tabular class.

rules.name: The Queried Figure Rule
rules.body: Figures on public surfaces come from the database. The ranked findings, the stat band, the readout and the demo control's label are all queried; linesRead() exists specifically so a lines-scanned figure cannot go stale. A rhetorical number above a measured one reads as a page that does not know its own figures.

rules.name: The Deterministic Scrim Rule
rules.body: Copy over the field always has its own ground. A fixed multi-stop gradient darkens the copy column, the right rail, and the top and bottom strips, so the field can stay vivid where there is nothing to read instead of being dimmed everywhere to protect text in one corner. "Mostly dark over there" is not a contrast guarantee when the field moves.

rules.name: The Margin Instrumentation Rule
rules.body: The edges carry readouts, not decoration: a numbered stage index left, a scroll rail and environment readout right, a live figure bottom-left in the loader's position.

rules.name: The Offset Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow that carries depth carries an offset and a blur. Zero-offset coloured halos are not a depth device in this system and must not be used to lift a surface, a control, or a panel. The only zero-offset glows in the build belong to emissive marks, where the glow is the light source itself and not the elevation.

rules.name: The Tonal First Rule
rules.body: Reach for the next ground and a hairline before reaching for a shadow. Three of the four shipped shadows are desktop-only or single-instance; the whole application shell has none.

rules.name: The Hairline Rectangle Rule
rules.body: Chrome is a hairline-bordered rectangle at 3px or less. The filled pill is the category's button and this world does not wear it.

rules.name: The Drawn Icon Rule
rules.body: Every icon is an SVG path at the set's stroke weight. →, ›, ✓ and ■ are text, and they render at whatever weight and baseline the resolved font chose — which is how the page once shipped two different arrows one line apart.

dos: Do spend ember only on the active state and the primary action, at most twice in a viewport.
Do write the band name beside every band mark; colour never carries meaning alone.
Do build chrome as hairline rectangles at 3px or less with a drawn arrow.
Do get condensed and extended from Archivo's wdth axis (64% display, 76–80% figures and headlines), not from a second family.
Do reserve JetBrains Mono for code, paths, line numbers, and scan output.
Do query every figure on a public surface from the database.
Do draw icons as SVG at the set's stroke weight.
Do separate cells with a 1px seam over edge before reaching for a border or a shadow.
Do put the gating decision before a heavy dynamic import, and give the declined path a composition-matching still rendition that costs zero bytes of the thing it declined.
Do give copy over the field its own deterministic scrim.
Do let a data failure cost a section its figures, never the page its composition.
donts: Don't use a filled pill as a control.
Don't introduce a fifth severity band; the ramp has four colours and no fifth one comes from the field.
Don't lift a surface or control with a zero-offset coloured halo; depth shadows carry offset and blur.
Don't use rounded-full on anything that is not a genuinely circular mark.
Don't let a unicode glyph stand in for an icon.
Don't reintroduce mint, green, or any warm hue other than ember; the grounds are cold by rule.
Don't build a feature section as a grid of equal icon-heading-body cards.
Don't ship a row of hero metrics in place of one resolved sentence.
Don't type a figure that the database can answer.
Don't make the conversion action the faintest element in a viewport.
Don't hide a loaded shader with a CSS class and call it gating.
Don't put a text colour under 4.5:1 on the void behind 11–13px type; faint is the floor and it is a role, not a licence.
